Keep them in one repo with full history, and set up new machines in minutes.
- [Fixing my broken Docker Immich+Traefik setup](https://subodhdahal.com/blog/fixing-docker-immich-traefik-setup.md): Photo indexing failed in my Immich+Traefik setup. I'd misconfigured my Docker networking. Here's how I figured it out and what I changed.

- [Quickly outline large JSON responses with a custom jq function](https://subodhdahal.com/blog/jq-json-outline.md): Use jq to automatically map and visualize the structure of large JSON responses, perfect for exploring undocumented endpoints.
- [Getting a Razer Core X eGPU to work after login on NixOS, without timing the boot](https://subodhdahal.com/blog/razer-core-x-egpu-hotplug-nixos.md)
- [Curating my own reading and discovery feed with RSS](https://subodhdahal.com/blog/reading-and-discovery-feed-curation.md): Taking concrete steps away from algorithms using FreshRSS, self-hosted tools, and a pipeline built for me.
- [Re-living memories through proper media organization](https://subodhdahal.com/blog/reliving-memories-through-proper-media-organization.md): Organizing media such as photos and videos can bring back cherished memories and help relive them. Here's my approach to organizing my digital media collection.
- [Self-Hosting my Git forge with Forgejo](https://subodhdahal.com/blog/self-hosting-my-git-forge.md): Why I moved away from GitHub and chose a lightweight, community-driven alternative
- [Why I added RSS feeds to my blog (and how I did it in Nuxt 3)](https://subodhdahal.com/blog/setting-up-rss-atom-feeds-nuxt3.md): How I built RSS and Atom feed support for my Nuxt 3 website to let readers follow my content without social media algorithms.
- [Revisiting my Stream Deck for music control](https://subodhdahal.com/blog/stream-deck-youtube-music.md): How I turned my neglected Stream Deck into a useful tool for controlling YouTube Music without breaking my workflow.
- [Stop stashing half-finished work: use Git worktrees and Worktrunk](https://subodhdahal.com/blog/worktrees-with-worktrunk.md): Git worktrees keep separate branches checked out at once. Worktrunk automates per-worktree setup. The same isolation also works for parallel AI agents.
